title: Pitfalls: holiday seasonality, regime change and incomplete data

videos.script: Every method in the last five lessons rests on one assumption. The future repeats the past, with noise. {{assumption}} This lesson is about the three most common ways that assumption breaks. {{three}} The first is the calendar. Carnival moved from February to March, and every comparison of February with last February came out wrong. {{calendar}} The second is the business. Panela raised its prices in September 2025, and the series stepped down to a new level. A model that does not know about the step reads it as something else. {{regime}} The third is the data itself. Yesterday's orders are not all in yet. A dashboard that shows them anyway announces a collapse that never happened. {{incomplete}} None of these is exotic. Each one happens to every business, every year. And each one is invisible to a method that was not told about it. {{invisible}} By the end of this lesson you will have found all three in Panela's data, fixed two, and have a checklist for the next series you forecast. {{end}}
